jobs.title: Audio AI Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation
jobs.description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation

Description

The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices, for applications such as dynamic awareness, hearing augmentation, agentic perception, voice pickup, content enhancement, and ones we haven’t even thought of yet. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms.

You will develop next-generation algorithms that isolate, extract, or suppress individual sound sources from microphone recordings, sometimes augmented by other sensor signals. Applications include voice pickup, hearing augmentation, and new audio experiences that must ultimately run in real time on physical devices.

Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next.

Responsibilities

Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel source separation and extraction algorithms for speech and other real-world sounds.
Develop approaches for single- and multi-microphone recordings, including spatial cues and optional auxiliary sensors.
Investigate robust separation in challenging conditions such as overlapping talkers, noise, reverberation, and motion.
Evaluate perceptual quality, separation performance, generalization, latency, memory, and computational requirements.
Collaborate with DSP and embedded software teams to deploy models in real-time demonstrations and product platforms; contribute to patents and conference papers.

Education

Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience.

Skills

Deep hands-on experience in audio source separation, target sound extraction, speech enhancement, or related neural audio processing.
Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution.
Strong knowledge of audio DSP, time-frequency methods, and microphone array or spatial signal processing.
Experience training and evaluating audio models in PyTorch; proficiency in Python and familiarity with C/C++ is a plus.
Understanding of objective and perceptual evaluation methods and the tradeoffs involved in real-time low-power inference.
Experience with multimodal or sensor-conditioned separation, ONNX/TFLite, or embedded deployment is a plus.
Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required.

At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves.

jobs.title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Overview

University Hospital Southampton is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us

Job Title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst

Contract Type: Permanent

Please be advised that this vacancy may close earlier than stated if we receive a large number of applications.

Main duties of the job

This is an exciting opportunity to join our growing Data & AI team within the Research & Development department at University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, as a Senior Research Analyst.

Working within the Southampton Emerging Therapies and Technologies (SETT) Centre, you will combine advanced analytical and data engineering expertise with line management responsibilities, leading a group of analysts and data engineers to deliver high-quality research data projects.

Our team supports clinical and academic research through the extraction, processing and analysis of routinely collected healthcare data, developing innovative tools and infrastructure to expand research capacity and improve patient outcomes.

You will play an important role in supporting research project delivery, ensuring technical quality, and working in the team to improve team processes and capabilities.

The SETT Data & AI team works to drive future transformation in patient care through the streamlined extraction of high quality data at scale, and the application of state of the art analytical techniques to drive research. By developing a data landscape friendly to research, we aim to expand Trust-wide research capacity and improve patient outcomes through helping to shape the future of medicine. This is a creative and rapidly evolving unit within the hospital’s R&D environment, and successful candidates will have the exciting opportunity to help shape its direction and long-term aims.

Working for our organisation

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated ‘Good’ by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the delivery of complex research data analysis projects within the Data & AI team. You will support project development and delivery, maintain high technical standards, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of the team's capabilities and working practices.

The Data & AI team works closely with clinical and academic researchers across University Hospital Southampton and partner organisations, supporting a diverse portfolio of research projects using routinely collected healthcare data. Our work ranges from developing automated data extraction and transformation pipelines to undertaking advanced analytical studies, building innovative research tools and improving the infrastructure that enables research at scale. Through this work, we aim to expand research capacity, support scientific discovery and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Research project development and delivery: Develop and manage a pipeline of research data projects, guiding enquiries from initial Expression of Interest through feasibility assessment, scoping, resource estimation and prioritisation into active delivery. Support the analytical delivery of allocated projects, monitoring progress, and working closely with researchers and research delivery teams to ensure projects meet their scientific and technical requirements.
Technical and analytical leadership: Undertake complex analyses of routinely collected NHS healthcare data, alongside the design and development of robust, reproducible data extraction, transformation and processing pipelines across clinical information systems. Provide technical oversight, including code review, testing, validation and documentation, while supporting the adoption of consistent technical standards and high-quality development practices.
Infrastructure, governance and service development: Contribute to the design and improvement of research data infrastructure, analytical tooling, development environments and automation capabilities to enable efficient and scalable study delivery. Help develop and embed team processes, policies and technical standards through knowledge-sharing, ensuring appropriate information governance and research compliance.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for a motivated and experienced analyst with an interest in advancing healthcare research.

The following skills and experience would position you well for this role:

Advanced analytical and engineering expertise: Educated to degree level in a numerate or scientific discipline, alongside substantial professional experience in data analysis or data engineering with strong SQL and Python skills, experience working with complex datasets, and a sound understanding of reproducible data processing, software development and quality assurance.
Project delivery and client-facing experience: Demonstrable experience of coordinating and delivering complex analytical or engineering projects in a client-facing environment, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders, understand requirements, assess feasibility, agree deliverables, manage expectations and communicate progress, supported by strong interpersonal, communication and relationship-management skills.
Technical judgement and continuous improvement: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, experience of handling sensitive information, an understanding of data protection and quality assurance requirements, and the ability to independently resolve technical challenges, improve working practices and support colleagues through knowledge-sharing and mentoring.

Person specification

Qualifications

Essential criteria

Educated to degree level or able to demonstrate equivalent level of knowledge/research experience relevant to the role.

Knowledge and Experience

Essential criteria

Significant experience of working with SQL to directly interrogate organisational data
Experienced use of Python programming in a working environment for engineering, data science or research
Experience of working with complex data across multiple disparate databases and multi-user environments, being able to demonstrate knowledge of these databases/ software.
Experience of medical research methodology and statutory clinical trial regulations, GCP and research governance requirements.
Experience of clinical trials in the NHS or the commercial health research sector.
Evidence of continuing professional development.
Evidence of ongoing/current Good Clinical Practice Training (GCP)
Thorough understanding of the systems and processes which are used to support the delivery of high quality clinical care in a research environment.
An understanding of R&D issues in the NHS.
Knowledge of research governance and quality assurance systems to ensure safe systems for patients.
Experience of previous training in monitoring of clinical research studies.
Knowledge of data governance requirements including GDPR

Desirable criteria

Commercial research experience.
Previous experience in using IRAS for R&D applications
Experience of working with additional programming languages
Experience of applying machine learning/LLMs within data engineering pipelines
Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or CI/CD development
Ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams, working with technical and non-technical persons
Experience of working collaboratively with version control tools such as Git

jobs.title: Research Associate
jobs.description:
Role Description

The Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) conducts policy-relevant environmental and sustainable development research. SEI York, one of nine SEI centres, has around 50 staff at the University of York. Our research spans air quality and climate change; nature-society relations; sustainable consumption and production; managing natural resources; and urban environments and human health. With a strong academic and international reputation, our credible, evidence-based research supports global decision-makers.

The Air quality, climate and environmental change group is seeking a research associate to support our work helping national Governments, cities and private sector companies identify, evaluate and prioritise actions that mitigate climate change and improve air quality and public health. Our group works with Governments to develop action plans and strategies that tackle Short-Lived Climate Pollutants. We support countries to develop Nationally Determined Contributions and other climate and air quality plans. We work with the private sector on air pollution mitigation with the Clean Air Fund (https://www.cleanairfund.org/) (CAF), United Nations Environment Programme, United Nations Global Compact and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (https://www.ccacoalition.org/en) (CCAC).

The group researches air pollution and climate change-related topics, develops guidance and tools relevant for Governments and companies and undertakes training and capacity building of relevant institutions for air pollution and climate change mitigation assessments. In 2022, SEI, collaborating with IKEA and CCAC, launched a guide targeted at businesses (https://www.ccacoalition.org/resources/practical-guide-business-air-pollutant-emission-assessment) to quantify value chain air pollution emission estimates, which is endorsed and used by members of the Alliance for Clean Air to quantify air pollutant emissions. We use tools like the Low Emissions Analysis Platform to help governments and cities to identify, evaluate and prioritise measures they can implement, and enhance the ability of decision makers to act. This tool is continuously enhanced by SEI US, and enables decision makers to develop their own mitigation models to inform their emission reduction planning. It has developed tools and methods to understand the broader socio-economic development benefits of taking action, designed to encourage policy coherence as the world grapples with health impacts of air pollution, climate change and achieving sustainable development goals.

The successful candidate will join a team of 10 researchers in developing our work researching air pollution, climate and health linkages, and working directly with countries and companies on their climate and air pollution planning. The candidate may also work with others in SEI, including those in our centres in Bangkok, Boston and Nairobi. Please refer to the job description for the main duties of the role.

Interview date: To be confirmed

To discuss this role informally, please contact Chris Malley at chris.malley@york.ac.uk.

Job Description

Abbott in Ireland

Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,500 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.

About Abbott

Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

About Abbott Vascular

Abbott Vascular is one of the world’s leading vascular care businesses, dedicated to advancing the treatment of vascular disease and improving patient outcomes worldwide. By combining cutting‑edge medical device innovation with world‑class pharmaceuticals, we invest heavily in research, development, training, and education to help shape the future of healthcare.

Our broad portfolio of vascular technologies—including vessel closure, endovascular, and coronary devices—helps treat diseases of the heart, carotid arteries, and peripheral blood vessels. These conditions can lead to heart attack, stroke, and other life‑threatening complications, making the work we do both meaningful and impactful.

At Abbott Clonmel, you’ll be part of a high‑performing manufacturing site where quality, innovation, and collaboration are at the core of everything we do.

Please note any offer of employment for this position is   conditional upon the successful completion   of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company.

new_jobs.title: Audio AI Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation
new_jobs.description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation

Description

The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices, for applications such as dynamic awareness, hearing augmentation, agentic perception, voice pickup, content enhancement, and ones we haven’t even thought of yet. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms.

You will develop next-generation algorithms that isolate, extract, or suppress individual sound sources from microphone recordings, sometimes augmented by other sensor signals. Applications include voice pickup, hearing augmentation, and new audio experiences that must ultimately run in real time on physical devices.

Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next.

Responsibilities

Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel source separation and extraction algorithms for speech and other real-world sounds.
Develop approaches for single- and multi-microphone recordings, including spatial cues and optional auxiliary sensors.
Investigate robust separation in challenging conditions such as overlapping talkers, noise, reverberation, and motion.
Evaluate perceptual quality, separation performance, generalization, latency, memory, and computational requirements.
Collaborate with DSP and embedded software teams to deploy models in real-time demonstrations and product platforms; contribute to patents and conference papers.

Education

Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience.

Skills

Deep hands-on experience in audio source separation, target sound extraction, speech enhancement, or related neural audio processing.
Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution.
Strong knowledge of audio DSP, time-frequency methods, and microphone array or spatial signal processing.
Experience training and evaluating audio models in PyTorch; proficiency in Python and familiarity with C/C++ is a plus.
Understanding of objective and perceptual evaluation methods and the tradeoffs involved in real-time low-power inference.
Experience with multimodal or sensor-conditioned separation, ONNX/TFLite, or embedded deployment is a plus.
Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required.

Role Description

The Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) conducts policy-relevant environmental and sustainable development research. SEI York, one of nine SEI centres, has around 50 staff at the University of York. Our research spans air quality and climate change; nature-society relations; sustainable consumption and production; managing natural resources; and urban environments and human health. With a strong academic and international reputation, our credible, evidence-based research supports global decision-makers.

The Air quality, climate and environmental change group is seeking a research associate to support our work helping national Governments, cities and private sector companies identify, evaluate and prioritise actions that mitigate climate change and improve air quality and public health. Our group works with Governments to develop action plans and strategies that tackle Short-Lived Climate Pollutants. We support countries to develop Nationally Determined Contributions and other climate and air quality plans. We work with the private sector on air pollution mitigation with the Clean Air Fund (https://www.cleanairfund.org/) (CAF), United Nations Environment Programme, United Nations Global Compact and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (https://www.ccacoalition.org/en) (CCAC).

The group researches air pollution and climate change-related topics, develops guidance and tools relevant for Governments and companies and undertakes training and capacity building of relevant institutions for air pollution and climate change mitigation assessments. In 2022, SEI, collaborating with IKEA and CCAC, launched a guide targeted at businesses (https://www.ccacoalition.org/resources/practical-guide-business-air-pollutant-emission-assessment) to quantify value chain air pollution emission estimates, which is endorsed and used by members of the Alliance for Clean Air to quantify air pollutant emissions. We use tools like the Low Emissions Analysis Platform to help governments and cities to identify, evaluate and prioritise measures they can implement, and enhance the ability of decision makers to act. This tool is continuously enhanced by SEI US, and enables decision makers to develop their own mitigation models to inform their emission reduction planning. It has developed tools and methods to understand the broader socio-economic development benefits of taking action, designed to encourage policy coherence as the world grapples with health impacts of air pollution, climate change and achieving sustainable development goals.

The successful candidate will join a team of 10 researchers in developing our work researching air pollution, climate and health linkages, and working directly with countries and companies on their climate and air pollution planning. The candidate may also work with others in SEI, including those in our centres in Bangkok, Boston and Nairobi. Please refer to the job description for the main duties of the role.

Interview date: To be confirmed

To discuss this role informally, please contact Chris Malley at chris.malley@york.ac.uk.

To pack and transport blood and blood products from the blood transfusion laboratory to clinical

areas and satellite blood fridges using the electronic blood management system.

To prioritise delivery of components to clinical areas based on urgency.
To periodically visit all the satellite blood banks on the SGH and PAH sites and return all unused

blood to the laboratory.

To maintain all UHS blood component storage facilities including cleaning and checking local and

remote alarm systems.

To collect blood and blood products from NHSBT including urgent ad hoc collections.
To escalate alarms and warnings generated by the electronic blood management system to a

registered healthcare scientist.

To complete daily data submissions for blood component stock and wastage to NHSBT via the

Vanessa platform.

Using templates from Charts issue letters to patients offering feotal RhD screening.
To complete weekly stock checks and escalate any deficiencies in stock to the advanced

Biomedical Scientists.

To receive deliveries into the department and complete the required documentation following

laboratory SOPs.

To carry out basic audits as directed by the Transfusion Laboratory Manager.
Demonstrate own working practices to new members of staff.
To maintain a personal training record to demonstrate competence and compliance with statutory

and mandatory training.

Job Description

Abbott in Ireland

Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,500 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.

About Abbott

Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

About Abbott Vascular

Abbott Vascular is one of the world’s leading vascular care businesses, dedicated to advancing the treatment of vascular disease and improving patient outcomes worldwide. By combining cutting‑edge medical device innovation with world‑class pharmaceuticals, we invest heavily in research, development, training, and education to help shape the future of healthcare.

Our broad portfolio of vascular technologies—including vessel closure, endovascular, and coronary devices—helps treat diseases of the heart, carotid arteries, and peripheral blood vessels. These conditions can lead to heart attack, stroke, and other life‑threatening complications, making the work we do both meaningful and impactful.

At Abbott Clonmel, you’ll be part of a high‑performing manufacturing site where quality, innovation, and collaboration are at the core of everything we do.

Please note any offer of employment for this position is   conditional upon the successful completion   of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company.

Key Responsibilities

Performs laboratory testing within a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) environment in support of one or more of the following areas; raw materials, in-process product, finished product, stability and/or validation
Manages laboratory samples by receiving, logging, labelling, preparing, storing, and disposing of samples and reagents in accordance with established procedures and laboratory requirements.
Provides laboratory support by maintaining clean and compliant work areas, preparing equipment, glassware and testing materials, assisting laboratory personnel with routine activities, and performing authorized laboratory tests and measurements as trained.
Perform analytical testing in accordance with GMP, laboratory procedures, and scientific principles to support product and material release.
Evaluate and interpret analytical data to ensure compliance with product specifications and identify potential quality concerns.
Recognise, investigate, document, and support resolution of deviations, OOS results, and exception events, including root cause analysis.
Maintain accurate, complete, and traceable laboratory documentation and records.
Prepare laboratory reagents, standards, and solutions in compliance with GMP requirements.
Ensure laboratory equipment is calibrated, maintained, and fit for purpose, including completion Of routine equipment checks.
Apply laboratory techniques and scientific principles effectively while troubleshooting technical and instrumentation issues as required.
Maintain compliance with safety, GMP, training, and procedural requirements, including appropriate use of PPE.
Manage workload effectively, prioritising tasks to meet business and o tional objectives.
Demonstrate proficiency in laboratory computer systems, data management tools, and standard office applications.
Support colleague training, knowledge sharing, and team development activities.
Participate in the review, update, and improvement of laboratory procedures, documentation, and processes.
Support I-IMS activities, including user support, issue resolution, training, compliance, business process improvements, and system development initiatives.
Adapt to changing priorities and work across multiple laboratory areas as required.
Demonstrate initiative, innovation, integrity, and teamwork through continuous improvement, accountability, collaboration, and positive engagement with colleagues.

Education and Job Skills :

(Experience/Education) National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ) level 6 qualification in a relevant discipline. Relevant work experience advantageous but not essential or an equivalent combination of education and work experience.
(Technical/Business Knowledge (Job Skills) Applies broad knowledge Of general technical concepts and practices and a general understanding of product or systems fundamentals. Utilises increased knowledge of numerical and statistical data and computer software programs to resolve non-routine/moderately complex problems. Will perform this job in a quality system environment. Failure to adequately perform tasks can result in noncompliance with governmental regulations.
(Cognitive Skills) Performs non-routine to moderately complex technical assignments using standard methods and sequences. Performs set-up, testing, repair, inspection, and/or maintenance of all area-specific equipment, materials, systems, and/or product. Makes adjustments, modifications, and replacements directed. Assignments require broad judgment in troubleshooting proven processes as well as the ability to suggest alternatives. Plans, organises, and prioritises own daily work routine to meet established schedule.
(Decision Making/lmpact) Solves a variety of problems of limited to moderate scope and complexity requiring basic interpretation of defined procedures and practices. Maintains confidentiality in handling sensitive information or documents.
(Supervision Received) General supervision. Receives general instruction On routine work and detailed instruction on new assignments
